title: Earnings Keep the Market Strong Despite Signs of Consumer Weakness | The Weekly Wrap

metadata.title: Earnings Keep the Market Strong Despite Signs of Consumer Weakness | The Weekly Wrap

summary: Eisman defends and adds to Charter after acknowledging a failed early turnaround signal, relying on future capex declines, buybacks and convergence. He sees continued AI infrastructure strength, uneven consumer conditions and a challenge to FICO pricing power. Charter's operating setback and the UAE's OPEC exit are verified. The multiyear Charter payoff and 2027 scoring transition remain open; private-software valuation extrapolations and broad causal market stories remain unresolved.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.
framework_points: Avoid changing a thesis merely because the stock moves.
Cheapness needs operating improvement or a cash-return catalyst.
Separate current loan performance from future refinancing exposure.
Distinguish aggregate consumer spending from individual household stress.
tools_and_charts: Charter capex schedule, free-cash-flow yield and buyback capacity.
Hyperscaler cloud growth and capital budgets.
transcript_cautions: Full transcript read, including extensive Charter update.
Forecast valuation multiples depend on future cash flows and ignore changing capital structure unless separately modeled.
Captioned hyperscaler revenue figures may omit or substitute segments; exact totals are not silently repaired.

claims.claim: Charter's poor quarter is a setback to his January recommendation, but he continues holding and added after the selloff rather than changing the original thesis.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.reason: The bad operating quarter is verified and acknowledged. His unchanged investment thesis is not a realized turnaround; transaction prices and position sizes are not independently verified.

evidence.title: Charter Q1 2026 results
evidence.finding: Internet customers declined 120,000; revenue fell 1%, adjusted EBITDA fell 2.2%, and FCF fell to $1.4b from $1.6b. The company repurchased 4.3m shares for $963m and reiterated longer-run improvement plans.

claims.next_check: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

claims.claim: Charter capex should fall substantially by 2028-2029, allowing enough free cash flow to retire roughly half its shares over four to five years.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.horizon: 2028-2029 capex and four to five years of buybacks
claims.test: Track actual capex, operating cash flow, debt requirements, repurchase prices and share count through 2030-2031; adjust for Cox transaction and dilution.
claims.reason: The stated future horizon or conditional scenario remains unfinished at the 2026-11-10 cutoff.
claims.next_check: Track actual capex, operating cash flow, debt requirements, repurchase prices and share count through 2030-2031; adjust for Cox transaction and dilution.

claims.claim: Charter's very low valuation implies excessive pessimism about capex, buybacks or EBITDA collapse, although cheapness alone cannot trigger returns.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

claims.claim: Converged broadband-mobile bundles and low pricing should eventually reverse Charter subscriber losses; he cannot time the turnaround.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare net Internet adds, mobile penetration, bundle profitability and cash returns over a specified horizon.
claims.reason: Q1 subscriber losses are real and Q3 still announces a plan to restore growth. The undefined horizon cannot be declared completed or automatically too early.

evidence.title: Charter Q1 2026 results
evidence.finding: Internet customers declined 120,000; revenue fell 1%, adjusted EBITDA fell 2.2%, and FCF fell to $1.4b from $1.6b. The company repurchased 4.3m shares for $963m and reiterated longer-run improvement plans.

evidence.title: Charter Q3 2026 results and new operating model
evidence.finding: Q3 legacy Charter Internet customers fell 156,000; combined pro forma customers fell 233,000 and adjusted EBITDA fell 4%. New operating model targets customer growth and $2b savings. Cox acquisition makes actual totals noncomparable; the earlier turnaround has not yet occurred.

claims.next_check: Compare net Internet adds, mobile penetration, bundle profitability and cash returns over a specified horizon.

claims.claim: The UAE's OPEC exit likely seeks production flexibility and market share, while its wider alliance implications are uncertain.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

evidence.title: UAE announces OPEC and OPEC+ exit
evidence.publisher: Emirates News Agency / UAE government statement
evidence.finding: Official withdrawal effective May 1; statement emphasizes production flexibility and gradual, demand-aligned additional supply. It does not establish hidden alliance motives.

claims.claim: Weak Domino's sales indicate lower-income stress even as AI investment supports the index and aggregate growth.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.reason: Later aggregate demand remained strong, consistent with uneven outcomes. One pizza chain does not establish that all lower-income households are in a deep recession, nor that AI alone produces GDP growth.

evidence.title: GDP advance estimate, third quarter 2026
evidence.finding: Real GDP increased 3.4% annualized in Q3; real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9% after 4.6% in Q2, with consumer goods and services both growing. This supports expansion through Q3, not a guarantee against future recession.
